name: dn-multi-ava-rdn-set-non-canonical-order-valid-rfc5280
description: Leaf subject has a multi-AVA RDN whose two AVAs are emitted in non-canonical SET order: OU=Engineering appears before O=Example, but DER SET ordering would put the shorter AttributeTypeAndValue first. The permitted directoryName constraint contains the same multi-AVA RDN but encoded canonically. RFC 5280 7.1 defines RDN equivalence as a set comparison (an RDN is an X.501 SET OF AttributeTypeAndValue), so semantically the two RDNs match and the leaf is inside the subtree.
notes: The leaf's subject is emitted via subject_der_ascii2der so the AVAs land in non-canonical SET order; cryptography's normal Name builder always sorts SET members canonically, which would erase the test. Strict DER validators may reject the cert outright; lenient BER decoders should still match the constraint after canonicalising on the fly. Either way is informative.

certs.subject: C=US,O=Example,CN=Alice
certs.subject_der_ascii2der: SEQUENCE { SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.6 } PrintableString { "US" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.11 } UTF8String { "Engineering" } } SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.10 } UTF8String { "Example" } } } SET { SEQUENCE { OBJECT_IDENTIFIER { 2.5.4.3 } UTF8String { "Alice" } } } }
